newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Rijksmuseum unearths rare Rembrandt drawing.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Rijksmuseum unearths rare Rembrandt drawing.

text.p: Amsterdam's Rijksmuseum said on Wednesday it had bought a rare drawing by Dutch Old Master Rembrandt, rediscovered by one of its experts after languishing unrecognised for decades in a private collection abroad.
The unsigned ink drawing, entitled "Portrait of actor Willem Bartolsz. Ruyter" and dated around 1638, goes on display at the museum on Thursday.
"It is extremely rare to turn up an undiscovered Rembrandt and this represents a very special find," museum spokesman Frans van der Avert said.
Peter Schatborn, head of the museum's drawings department, identified the portrait as a Rembrandt from a photocopy sent to him by an unnamed foreign collector, Van der Avert said.
"The unrecognised drawing had been in his family for two generations. Before then it was last seen and identified as a Rembrandt in Vienna in the early 19th century."
Van der Avert said the portrait had great art historical value because it enabled the identification of a subject used by Rembrandt in numerous other works.
Drawings featuring the actor in different guises are contained in the collections of London's Victoria and Albert Museum, Berlin's Kupferstichkabinett and the Duke of Devonshire.
